headline: The US government's audit agency found that none of 24 major federal agencies had fully prepared to move its systems to encryption that resists quantum computers.
score_reason: Pool score 5, lowered by 1: the GAO report came out on 6 Oct 2026, a week before the window, though the findings are accurately stated.
importance_line: Federal systems that hold sensitive data are exposed to a future quantum attack and agencies face a 22 Oct 2026 planning deadline, but the audit ended in September 2025, so agencies may have made progress since.
summary: eWeek reports on a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report, made public on 6 Oct 2026, which found that none of the 24 federal agencies covered by the Chief Financial Officers Act had fully prepared for post-quantum cryptography, meaning encryption built to resist quantum computers. Only one had a complete inventory of vulnerable systems, none had fully accurate cost estimates and none had tested the new algorithms; the audit ended in September 2025, before the June 2026 executive orders.
